inputs.share_count_basis: 54,567,627 common shares outstanding at 2026-08-04 (Q2-2026 report cover). Basic and diluted EPS are identical in every year FY2021-FY2025 (FY2025 diluted weighted average 55.37m), so basic = fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is charged inside adjusted EBITDA, and the company repurchases (C$90m FY2024, C$90m FY2025, C$20m H1-2026).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report employee-benefit note: share-based compensation expense C$14m (FY2024 C$14m), of which ~C$9m equity-settled (TRSU/TPSU) and the rest cash-settled (DSU/RSU liabilities, remeasured to share price). The cash-flow add-back is net-negative in H1-2026 (-5), i.e. the cash-settled part is real cash inside OCF. last_fcf deducts the ~C$9m equity-settled portion from reported FCF (OCF 557 - PP&E capex 103 = 454). No net-share-settlement tax line is disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0 every year). Forward: the company's adjusted EBITDA is operating income + D&A + impairment/restructuring and does NOT add back SBC, so the projected EBITDA margin is already post-SBC; sbc_pct_path is held at 0 to avoid charging it twice.
inputs.fx_note: None needed. Statements are 'in millions of Canadian dollars' (Q2-2026 MD&A, FY2025 annual report) and SJ trades on the TSX in CAD (Yahoo SJ.TO currency CAD). ~76% of sales are US-sourced and translated to CAD; that is translation exposure inside the flows, not a reporting/quote mismatch.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CAD, the flows' currency. Risk-free ~3.3% (10y Government of Canada), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0 for a cyclical-exposed industrial (residential lumber, rail ties) -> cost of equity ~8.3-8.8%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (revolver/term loans/notes), ~3.7% after 26% tax. Target weights ~70/30 equity/debt (debt C$1.35bn vs market cap ~C$3.5bn) -> ~7.2%; rounded to 7.5%. Same WACC in every scenario: risk is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Lease cash (principal C$66m + interest C$11m = C$77m FY2025, ~2.2% of sales; mainly leased railcars and rolling stock) is deducted through lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (C$300m at 2026-06-30) are EXCLUDED from net debt; net debt = long-term debt incl. current portion C$1,346m less cash C$138m. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 D&A 145 less ROU depreciation 68 = 77; H1-2026 PP&E dep 30 + intangibles amortization 15 annualizes to ~90, higher after Brooks), so the lease is not charged twice in the cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: None: no non-controlling interests in the consolidated statements; flows are 100% attributable.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (engine route) with the non-US/cyclical adaptations, chosen because Stella-Jones is an ordinary operating manufacturer (treated-wood utility poles, rail ties, residential lumber, steel transmission structures) whose value is its free cash flow; none of the bank/REIT/holdco/distressed routes apply. First valuation of this ticker; no prior model to match. Base anchor is UNDERLYING FY2025, not reported: FY2025 EBITDA of C$661m included a C$28m insurance settlement gain (2023 fire) -> underlying C$633m, 18.1% of sales. FY2026 is the guidance year: H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA margin 16.5% (Q2 16.0%) on site-specific environmental/maintenance costs, fuel, steel-facility modernization inefficiency and pricing lag; management says full-year 2026 adjusted margin will be BELOW 17.5% and expects a return into the 17.5-18.5% target range over the 2026-2028 outlook period (Q2-2026 report, CEO letter, 2026-08-06). 2026-2028 objectives (Nov-2025 investor day): ~C$4bn sales by 2028 including acquisitions, 17.5-18.5% adjusted EBITDA margin, net debt/EBITDA 2.0-2.5x. Base case reaches ~C$3.9bn by 2028 and 17.5% - i.e. below the sales target and at the bottom of the margin range, because rail ties are shrinking (CPKC insourcing, four Class-1 contracts renewing in 2026) and residential lumber prices are weak. Q2-2026 C$32m impairment/restructuring (rail-tie network optimization) is non-recurring and excluded from margins. Working capital: inventory-heavy manufacturer (inventory C$1.55bn = ~43% of sales; seasonal, pole/tie air-drying) so growth CONSUMES cash: wc_capture -30% of each revenue increase. FY2025 reported FCF (C$454m) is flattered by a C$95m working-capital release (inventory -85) and is not a base; FY2023 was -48 on an inventory build. Capex: FY2025 C$103m PP&E plus ~C$9m intangibles; 2026-27 carry the US$50m Fayetteville TN steel-lattice greenfield (approved 2026-02-25) and the Candiac expansion, so capex is 4.2%/4.0% of sales before settling to ~3.0% (maintenance ~2.5% + growth). Cash tax 24%: FY2025 taxes paid C$92m vs expense C$110m on a 26.1% Canadian statutory / ~25% US blended rate. Buybacks fund the flat share count (repurchaser).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 8.2% is >30% below EPS 5yr CAGR 14.3%: EPS growth was boosted by buybacks (shares 67.3m FY2020 -> 55.3m FY2025) and by the FY2023-24 margin step-up from ~14.5% to ~18%, which management now says will not hold in FY2026. Revenue 5yr CAGR 6.5% includes acquisitions. The forward revenue path (2-4.5% then 2.5%) is set from guidance and segment trends, not from either CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs end FY2025 (3yr from FY2022, 5yr from FY2020). FCF CAGRs use owner FCF (reported FCF less ~equity-settled SBC; SBC is small, 0.4% of sales, so owner and reported FCF track closely) and are meaningless as growth rates: they are driven by working-capital swings (FY2022 owner FCF ~151 after an inventory build, FY2025 ~445 after a C$95m release). SBC is not growing faster than cash flow.

base.narrative: Utility poles grow mid-single digits on grid hardening and replacement, steel structures (Locweld, Brooks, Fayetteville from 2027-28) add growth, rail ties shrink low single digits as CPKC insources and Class-1 renewals reprice, residential lumber stays flat near C$600-650m. FY2026 margin 16.8% (below the 17.5% floor, as guided), recovering to the bottom of the 17.5-18.5% target by 2028 and held there.

bull.narrative: Management delivers the 2026-2028 plan: ~C$4bn sales by 2028 with utility pole volume and pricing strong on grid-hardening and wildfire-resilience spend, steel lattice demand from transmission build-out filling Candiac and Fayetteville, Class-1 tie contracts renewed at stable volume, and network optimization plus pricing pass-through restoring margin to the top of the 17.5-18.5% range.

bear.narrative: The FY2023-25 ~18% margin proves to have been a utility-pole pricing peak: spot pole prices keep normalizing, more Class-1 railroads follow CPKC into in-house tie treating or reprice the 2026-27 renewals, residential lumber stays depressed, and cost inflation is not recovered. Margin settles at 15.5%, between the FY2021-22 ~14.5% and today, with near-flat sales.

scenario_narratives.base: Utility-led mid-single-digit growth offset by a shrinking rail-tie book and flat residential lumber; FY2026 adjusted EBITDA margin ~16.8% (management: below 17.5%), back to 17.5% by 2028 and held at the bottom of the target range. Sales reach ~C$3.9bn in 2028, short of the ~C$4bn objective.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 2026-2028 objectives are met in full: ~C$4bn sales in 2028, margin at 18.5% as network optimization, pricing pass-through and the steel structures ramp (Candiac, Fayetteville) land, and the 2026 Class-1 tie renewals hold volume.
scenario_narratives.bear: Peak-margin unwind: pole pricing normalizes further, rail insourcing spreads beyond CPKC and the 2026-27 renewals reprice, residential lumber stays weak; margin settles at 15.5% on near-flat sales.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: management has just cut the FY2026 margin outlook below its own range, four Class-1 tie contracts renew in 2026 against an active insourcing precedent (CPKC), and customer concentration is high. Base 50%: guidance-consistent recovery to the bottom of the target range. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things at once (full margin recovery, steel ramp on time, renewals at volume, lumber recovery).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Stella-Jones is a maintenance-replacement infrastructure supplier with a cyclical tail (residential lumber, pole pricing). Value rests on whether the FY2023-25 ~18% EBITDA margin is the new normal or a pricing peak; the base case accepts management's recovery to only the bottom of its 17.5-18.5% range, and the bear case prices a reversion toward the pre-2023 mid-teens. Working capital is a real growth cost (inventory ~43% of sales), so reported FCF in release years overstates the run-rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Class-1 railway tie renewals in 2026-27 and further railroad insourcing of tie treatment (CPKC precedent)
Utility pole spot-price normalization eroding the post-2023 margin step-up
Margin recovery to 17.5% by 2028 depends on cost recovery through pricing mechanisms and network optimization
Residential lumber price and demand cyclicality
Execution on the Fayetteville steel greenfield and Candiac expansion
Inventory-driven working-capital swings make any single year's FCF unrepresentative
USD/CAD translation: ~76% of sales and most debt are USD
